subsystems.name: Ingestible nanostructures
subsystems.role: the sensing elements that circulate in the bloodstream or attach to tissues.
parts: molecular recognition coatings (antibodies, aptamers, imprinted polymers)

subsystems.name: Power and activation
subsystems.role: supplies energy or triggers sensing without a battery.

subsystems.name: Communication link
subsystems.role: gets data out of the body through tissue.

subsystems.name: Molecular sensing
subsystems.role: detects specific molecules at low concentration.
parts: receptors for proteins, metabolites, nucleic acids

subsystems.name: Biocompatibility and clearance
subsystems.role: ensures the particles are safe and leave the body.

subsystems.name: Data system
subsystems.role: turns streams of ultrasound signals into health telemetry.
parts: secure data transmission to phone or cloud

buildSteps.title: Design the sensor chemistry
buildSteps.detail: Choose target molecules and match them with receptors that bind selectively in blood or tissue.

buildSteps.title: Synthesize nanostructures
buildSteps.detail: Create cores of biodegradable or inert material with tightly controlled size and shape.

buildSteps.title: Functionalize surfaces
buildSteps.detail: Attach receptors and protective coatings that resist fouling and immune attack.

buildSteps.title: Assemble into an ingestible capsule
buildSteps.detail: Package the nanostructures in a pill that releases them at a chosen point in the gut.

buildSteps.title: Build the external transducer system
buildSteps.detail: Design a wearable ultrasonic array that powers the particles and reads their backscattered signals.

buildSteps.title: Test in vitro and in animals
buildSteps.detail: Validate sensitivity, specificity, safety, and how quickly the particles are cleared.

buildSteps.title: Run human trials and seek approval
buildSteps.detail: Demonstrate clinical utility and safety in people before any routine use.

prerequisites.tech: Ultrasonic power and communication through tissue
prerequisites.why: research has shown ultrasound can power and read implants, but not yet swarms of nanoscale particles.
many biosensors work in the lab, but continuous real-time detection in blood is still difficult.
several nanoparticles are approved for drug delivery, though not for sensing swarms.
simple nanoparticles are made in bulk, but complex multifunctional ones remain costly and inconsistent.
no proven way exists to remove thousands of nanobots safely after they have done their job.

pathway.milestone: ingestible sensors for specific markers such as pH, temperature, or gas with ultrasonic or radio readout
pathway.unlocks: proof that internal telemetry can work reliably.

pathway.milestone: biodegradable nanoparticles that report a few molecular targets when activated by an external ultrasound patch
pathway.unlocks: continuous monitoring of key biomarkers without permanent implants.

pathway.milestone: swarms of nanobots that circulate, sense many molecules, and are cleared naturally
closed-loop system that senses and delivers drugs automatically
